title: One Lane, Then Sit
hook: Two lanes left look faster. They are not one move.
scene: Overcast midday on I-90 east, three lanes this way. You are in the right. A slow box is ahead in your lane. The left two look empty enough to steal. The side-street move is to cut both in one sweep and be done. At this speed each lane is a sentence. The second lane cannot hear a stalk that already died on the first.
decision: You need left of this box. How many lanes do you take?

options.text: Sweep left across both empty lanes in one motion and sit in the leftmost
options.result: You cut two. A sedan you did not own was filling the middle. He lifts. One stalk cannot buy two lanes at this speed.

options.text: Pass him on the right shoulder so you never change lanes at all
options.result: The shoulder is a drain and a post. You put the plow in the junk to skip a legal change.

options.text: Take the middle, sit until the box is in the right glass, then take the left
options.result: One lane. You sit. The box shows in the right door glass. Then the next lane, its own stalk, its own gap. Two sentences. Nobody lifted.

options.text: Hold the right and wait until the slow box exits so you never pass
options.result: He is through traffic. He does not exit. You travel his number for miles and the schedule pays for a pass you were allowed to take one lane at a time.

debrief: Change one lane at a time. Sit until the last lane is yours. You took one lane and sat.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part two
source.teaching_target: On the highway, change lanes one at a time only.
